claim: A commanded continuous reset arrives as an ordinary `Bool` input; weight-on-wheels is the shipped instance.
fix: where the reset command arrives as an ordinary `Bool` input (weight-on-wheels is the canonical case, and the `reset` input of `Integrator(; reset = true)` the shipped instance)
ver_evidence: The mechanism matches: src/library.jl:454 reset_guard(_, (; u)) = u.reset, and src/library.jl:965 Integrator{V, true} declares state_events (reset = StateEvent(reset_guard, reset_handler),), so the reset arrives as a Bool input and fires through an event guard. But nothing in src/, test/ or examples/ ships weight-on-wheels (rg -i 'weight.on|wheels|wow|strut' finds nothing). The shipped instances are Integrator(; reset = true) and LimitedIntegrator (src/library.jl:1878). The gear and PIVector belong to the planned Flight.jl migration (design/companions/migration_outline.md:71-90), and no pending.md bullet owes them.

claim: The build reads each contract declaration once, against the concrete instance, so a value-dependent contract does not announce itself.
fix: The build reads each declaration against the concrete instance alone and never compares instances of one type, so a value-dependent contract does not announce itself.
ver_evidence: Probe SA-051a: building one model with two instances of one type VD, whose u_types depends on a field value, succeeds silently, as the doc says. But during that build the build calls u_types 19 times. Probe SA-051b: Simulation plus init! call it twice more. The build reads a declaration many times, at each pass that needs it, for example src/declare.jl:860-871, src/build.jl:545 and :879, src/assembly.jl:409 and :776. What holds is that every read is against the concrete instance and no read compares instances of one type. "Once" is literally false.

claim: Relative and Absolute arguments are each an integer or a Rational
fix: Sample-time entries. `Relative(D, Φ = 0)` in scope ticks, its child's `Dₛ` and `Φₛ`, each an integer, and `Absolute(Δt, τ = 0)` in exact rational seconds, each an integer or a `Rational` ([§8.7][s8-7], [D-185][d-185], [D-469][d-469], [D-478][d-478]).
ver_evidence: src/declare.jl:438-441: Relative takes only Integer counts and throws ArgumentInvalid :not_a_count for any other Real; probe.jl:28-29 Relative(2//1) and Relative(1//2) both throw :not_a_count, while probe.jl:30-31 show Absolute taking Rationals of any integer type. The spec body (design/spec.md:4415-4417) and the D-459 annotation (design/log.md:19655-19663) say Relative refuses a rational.
ver_note: The ruling (commit 2797c742, 2026-11-14, D-459 annotation, §8.7) came before this Appendix B sentence was rewritten in 5ed966f6 (D-469, 2026-11-20). That rewrite let 'each an integer or a Rational' cover Relative too. The code follows the ruling.

claim: LevenbergMarquardt() takes no keywords (leads: maxiter and λ₀ are code-only)
fix: `LevenbergMarquardt(; maxiter = 100, λ₀ = 1e-3)`, the default backend, is an in-house dense Levenberg–Marquardt, `maxiter` its iteration cap and `λ₀` its starting damping ([§14.8][s14-8], [D-070][d-070]).
ver_evidence: src/trim.jl:282 LevenbergMarquardt(; maxiter::Integer = 100, λ₀::Real = 1e-3), documented as keywords in its docstring (src/trim.jl:270-274); probe.jl:86 => ([:maxiter, :λ₀], LevenbergMarquardt(5, 1.0)). Neither keyword appears anywhere in design/spec.md, design/log.md or design/pending.md.
ver_note: Appendix B lists other constructors' keywords (BS3, Deployment), so leaving these two out reads as 'no keywords'. Whether they are public is a §14.8 ruling, not only an Appendix B edit. λ₀ ≤ 0 is also refused as a raw ArgumentError (src/trim.jl:283), not as ArgumentInvalid.

claim: a cell is one per output port of the flattened model
fix: one concretely typed entry of the [signal table](#g-signal-table), one per output [port](#g-port) of the flattened model, written by its producing stage, plus one per [root input](#g-root-input), a source cell the periphery feeds, read by every gatherer ([§4.1][s4-1]).
